boundaries.label: Existing Python control-plane worker — proposed DBOS library, initial single executor

cards.title: Why DBOS is the candidate for this project
items: Durable Python workflows and queues checkpoint into PostgreSQL. The open-source library needs no separate orchestration server.
Reuse the existing database and Python worker. This targets low initial operational overhead; no cost/performance benchmark has been run.
The generic queued workflow was approved. Selecting DBOS is this new proposal; no library, migration, paid service or deployment has been installed.

cards.title: Framework owns scheduling; product owns correctness
items: DBOS owns durable queue/checkpoint state and configured step retries/backoff. Single-executor interrupted workflows recover on restart.
P17 owns authentication, current project/attempt checks, confirmed cleanup handoff, evidence integrity, criteria rules, cancellation and terminal receipts.
PASS/FAIL are result data, not retry signals. Only explicit transient exceptions retry within bounded policies; repeated delivery still requires idempotent product writes.

cards.title: Atomic acceptance and safe recovery
items: DBOS Client enqueue_in_transaction can use the caller-owned SQLAlchemy transaction when both schemas are in the same logical database; the async caller uses run_sync.
Seal frozen inputs, save the acceptance receipt and enqueue the DBOS workflow together, then return 202. No custom outbox/queue poller is proposed.

Workflow payloads/checkpoints carry bounded identifiers/digests, not credentials or raw telemetry. Final commit rechecks current cancellation/terminal/evidence guards; cached steps never grant fresh authorization.

cards.title: Reliability limits and the preserved lifecycle gate
items: Initial scope: one control-plane workflow executor plus durable PostgreSQL and process restart management. No automatic multi-worker high-availability claim.
DBOS distributed crash recovery needs coordination, for example Conductor or explicit recovery operations. That rollout choice remains a separate reviewed decision.
Runner cleanup and sealing close execution write rights; server processing uses its own deadline. Keep expiry maintenance responsive and preserve terminal results.
Temporal remains an alternative with its own service; Redis alone is a datastore, typically paired with a task framework such as Celery. This proposal adds neither.
